subject: gov.policy
name: African Development Bank Country Strategy Paper 2026-2031
milestone: Approved February 2026 and launched in Monrovia, 30 July 2026
position_start: Bank strategy carrying four sectors, ICT among them (2025-08)
position_end: Sectors cut from four to three - transport, energy and skills - with an indicative 2026-2028 programme of UA 129m (US$172.86m, February 2026 conversion), 36.3% unfunded, and no digital lending line (2026-07)
note: The strategy's own ICT assessment still cites the National ICT Policy and Strategy 2019-2024 and does not mention the Digital Liberia strategy published the same month.

subject: gov.policy
name: Cloud-first government hosting policy
milestone: Named in the 2026-2029 infrastructure roadmap
position_start: No published position on government hosting (2025-08)
position_end: A cloud-first policy and a government network named in the national infrastructure roadmap, with no instrument, standard or timetable published (2026-04)

subject: gov.policy
name: Digital Liberia national digital strategy 2025-2029
milestone: Published by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, February 2026
position_start: National ICT Policy and Strategy 2019-2024, already past its stated period (2025-08)
position_end: Eight priority areas across four pillars, including universal connectivity, digital addressing, cybersecurity and data sovereignty; no costing or delivery schedule published (2026-02)
sources: 2026-02-03 Liberia Unveils 5-Year 'Digital Liberia' Strategy to Boost Sovereignty and Innovation|2026-02-03 Liberia National Digital Strategy 2025-2029 (Digital Liberia)

subject: gov.policy
name: National broadband expansion plan
milestone: Committed for years 2-4 of the 2026-2029 infrastructure roadmap
position_start: Broadband targets carried by the National ICT Policy 2019-2024, past its stated period (2025-08)
position_end: No separately titled national broadband strategy; the January 2026 infrastructure conference roadmap commits the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications and the LTA to a national broadband expansion plan in years 2-4 (2026-04)

subject: gov.policy
name: National Data Governance Policy
milestone: Final version issued by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, March 2026
position_end: Final policy designating the Independent Information Commission as data regulator under the unenacted Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act 2024, prescribing signature and ratification of the Malabo Convention, and setting an adequacy-or-explicit-consent rule for personal data leaving the country (2026-03)
note: Developed under ministry leadership with CIPESA and aligned to the African Union Data Policy Framework.

subject: gov.policy
name: Payment-system local hosting requirement (CBL/RSD/003/2020)
milestone: Gazetted 8 January 2020
position_end: Section 9(c) states the payment system should be hosted locally and, where hosted abroad, obliges the licensee to give the central bank unfettered access - a sectoral norm with an offshore escape, not an economy-wide localisation regime

subject: gov.policy
name: Telecommunications authority strategic plan 2025-2029
milestone: Plan published in abridged form
position_end: The telecommunications regulator's five-year plan, named as the anchor of its current agenda. The version the base holds is an abridged, infographic-led edition in which most of the substantive content - situational analysis, stakeholder analysis and target tables - is laid out as designed graphics rather than extractable text
note: the plan is the regulator's stated agenda and its targets cannot be read off the only version published; the acting chairperson's programme - internet access for schools and underserved communities, consumer protection, cybersecurity - is described in press accounts rather than against the document

subject: gov.legislate
name: Artificial intelligence legislation or regulation
status: Not held, searched 2026-09-04 - no AI-specific instrument or evidentiary rule located
milestone: No instrument found
position_end: Still none: a criminal court ruled on alleged AI-generated audio in December 2025 on ordinary disclosure grounds with no AI-specific rule applied, and the Executive Mansion's July 2026 warning on fabricated documents is an authentication appeal rather than a rule

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic Transactions Law 2002 (Chapter 13, Title 14)
milestone: Approved 8 January 2002, published 19 June 2002
position_end: Liberia's only enacted electronic-commerce statute; nothing covering online consumer protection, platforms or intermediary liability has been enacted since 2002

subject: gov.legislate
name: LTA licensing and spectrum reform package
milestone: Reform package set out by the board chair, 17 July 2026
position_start: Licensing under the Telecommunications Act 2007 unchanged, with no satellite or device rules (2025-08)
position_end: Split of infrastructure and service licences, tower-sharing rules, first satellite regulations, an IMEI regime and repatriation of the .lr country domain announced; none published as instruments (2026-07)

subject: gov.legislate
name: Mobile Money Regulations (Central Bank of Liberia)
milestone: In force as the central bank's mobile-money framework
position_end: In force and unamended; the interoperable fee schedule of 2026 was approved under it (2026-08)
sources: 2024-01-01 Liberia Mobile Money Regulations (Central Bank of Liberia)

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Identification Registry Act 2011
milestone: Approved 1 August 2011, published 8 August 2011
position_end: In force: repeals PRC Decree 65, creates the autonomous National Identification Registry and makes the National Biometric Identification System, the biometric card and the Social Security Number the primary government identity number

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Statistics and Geo-Information Act 2004
milestone: Approved 22 July 2004
position_end: In force and unamended; the House summoned the statistics office in June 2026 to justify the population benchmarks behind a proposed expansion from 73 to 87 seats

subject: gov.legislate
name: Satellite Communications Guidelines (LTA-GL-002-2026)
milestone: Licensing, tax and service rules set out for the satellite market
position_end: The regulator has set the rules of the satellite telecommunications market through its 2026 satellite communications guidelines, framing licensing, taxation and service obligations around national security and commercial transparency as space-based solutions become the route to reaching territories terrestrial networks have not
note: the regulator frames it as opening licensed satellite broadband to the named constellations; no licence has yet been issued under it on the record

subject: gov.protect
name: Data sharing arrangement under the health memorandum
status: Planned, deferred to an unpublished appendix
milestone: Deferred to an unpublished Appendix 5
position_end: A rights organisation's reading of the seven signed American health memoranda puts Liberia among three that commit to hand over any data requested for the American audit without explicit privacy safeguards, and among two whose data-sharing arrangement is deferred to an unpublished appendix; Liberia is outside the five whose text requires unilateral specimen and pathogen-sequencing sharing, and the signed memorandum carries no specimen clause
note: the same reading names Liberia as lacking a binding comprehensive data-protection law, which is what makes the audit-access provision acute; the appendix itself is not published

subject: gov.protect
name: Personal Information Act (data protection bill)
milestone: Signed into force alongside the cybercrime law 2026-08-19
position_start: Referred to a House committee in June 2025, unpassed, with no national data authority (2025-08)
position_end: Signed into force on 2026-08-19; no data-protection authority yet exists to administer it
sources: 2026-08-20-wearetech-liberia-cybercrime-data-protection-laws|2025-06-11-house-reviews-privacy-data-protection-bill-observer|2026-05-16 World Bank, African DPAs outline formula for trusted digital identity, DPI|2025-02-27 Liberia struggles to enforce privacy and data protection laws
note: Drafted with Internews under the EU media programme and validated in December 2024; Liberia is an ECOWAS data-protection signatory. The law is now in force, but the base holds no authority, commencement order, registration regime or enforcement route under it, so what a data subject can do with it is unestablished

subject: gov.protect
name: Privacy enforcement against telecom operators
milestone: Orange Liberia fined LRD 4m for unauthorised issuance of a subscriber's SIM to a third party
position_start: Did not exist; no privacy penalty on record (2025-08)
position_end: LRD 4m fine (US$21,900 at the time, per the source) imposed by the telecoms regulator rather than under data-protection law (2026-06)

subject: gov.regional
name: African Telecommunications Union membership
milestone: US$361,151.36 in arrears waived and voting rights restored at the Abuja plenipotentiary session, July 2026
position_start: Voting rights withheld over arrears dating back to 1982 (2025-08)
position_end: Arrears waived, current obligations arranged, ratification instrument deposited and voting rights restored (2026-07)

subject: gov.regional
name: Liberia-Gambia-Sierra Leone free roaming
milestone: Took effect 2 May 2025
position_start: In effect, home SIM at local rates across the three countries (2025-08)
position_end: In effect; no traffic or price data published (2026-08)

subject: gov.regional
name: Study visit to the Rwandan e-government model
milestone: One of eight delegations hosted in a single week
position_end: A government delegation was among eight from seven African countries hosted by Rwanda's cooperation agency in a single week at the end of August 2026, several of them studying its e-government model; some delegations travelled with the World Bank, the United Nations Development Programme or a private consultancy
note: the account names this country among the delegations without describing what its own delegation studied or what followed; no agreement, programme or replication commitment is recorded

subject: gov.regional
name: West African banking supervision and cyber resilience cooperation
milestone: Central bank governor's call at a CSWAMZ virtual meeting 2026-08-19
position_end: Proposed: shared cybersecurity standards, cross-border incident reporting and supervisory-technology adoption among West African regulators
note: the central bank governor's call at a College of Supervisors of the West African Monetary Zone virtual meeting, citing Liberia's own instant-payment launch of December 2025 as a domestic benchmark; nothing is adopted, funded or scheduled, and the proposal is one governor's rather than the college's position

subject: gov.standards
name: ePhyto electronic phytosanitary certificate exchange
milestone: Launched 20 April 2026
position_end: Live on the IPPC and FAO ePhyto hub under the Regional ePhyto Africa Window, replacing paper certification (2026-04)

subject: gov.standards
name: Liberia Standards Authority
milestone: Established by Act signed 5 August 2022
position_end: The apex national standards body, grounded expressly in the ECOWAS quality infrastructure (ECOQUAL, ECOSHAM, Regulation C/REG.19/12/13) and World Trade Organization technical-barriers obligations
note: Capture is an excerpt: the source scan yielded only the preamble and enacting clause.

subject: gov.standards
name: National Numbering Plan
milestone: Adopted by the LTA, December 2023
position_end: Adopts ITU-T Recommendation E.164 for national number structure and E.212 for mobile country and network codes, giving an international standard domestic legal effect

subject: gov.discourse
name: Anti-Corruption Commission complaint against the LTA
milestone: Complaint forwarded to the Commission's investigation unit, 30 July 2026
position_end: Under investigation, with no evidence publicly produced and no findings made (2026-07)

subject: gov.discourse
name: Disclosure of telecommunications sector revenue
milestone: Acting chairperson summoned to the Executive Mansion
position_end: The telecommunications regulator is under executive scrutiny over undisclosed revenue activities, its acting chairperson summoned to the Executive Mansion after the president raised concern at the regulator's recurring appearance in the media over revenue questions and urged transparency. Civil society and media have pressed for months for disclosure of sector revenue and how it is accounted for; the chairperson has maintained he is accountable to the president. Commissioners hold tenured positions removable only for established cause, and the recent court acquittal of a former chairman suspended over corruption allegations has sharpened scrutiny of the regulator's independence
note: no sector revenue figure, audit or disclosure instrument is published, so the dispute is about the absence of a number rather than about its size; the account rests on unnamed sources

subject: gov.discourse
name: Police connectivity and vehicle procurement statement
milestone: Statement issued 21 August 2026
position_end: The national police said on 21 August 2026 that none of its facilities use satellite internet and that its connectivity is supplied by the state operator under an official institutional contract; it confirmed that it bought used operational vehicles from a US firm, and said its institutional records do not support claims linking either arrangement to individuals in the country's narcotics investigation
note: a denial rather than a disclosure: no contract, value or procurement record is published alongside it

subject: gov.discourse
name: Statutory consultation duty on telecommunications policy
milestone: Sections 7(1) and 11(4), Telecommunications Act 2007
position_end: In force and exercised: the LTA opened a formal consultation on satellite communications guidelines on 23 February 2026 with a public forum, a comment deadline and a published consultation report

subject: gov.discourse
name: U-Report youth feedback platform
milestone: Relaunched 2026-08-13
position_end: Relaunched by UNICEF and UNFPA with support from the Irish embassy under a joint programme with the government, giving young people an encrypted SMS channel on one operator's network to answer polls on health, water and sanitation and other social issues, with responses analysable by county and a target of at least 8,000 reporters
note: the channel is tied to a single mobile operator's SIM cards, which bounds who can take part; no baseline participation figure or publication rule for the results is stated

subject: finance.budget
name: Universal Access Fund (LTA-REG-0006)
milestone: Regulations made September 2015
position_end: Funded by a licensee contribution set at 0.5 per cent of annual gross revenues, with annual legislative approval for disbursement; its most recent published deployment is a satellite installation in Vahun District, Lofa County

subject: finance.mou
name: Cybaston Digital Fast Track master agreement
milestone: Signed 23 September 2024
position_end: A five-year master service framework covering undersea capacity of up to 1 Tbps, a data centre for consolidated e-government services, e-visa, e-tax and e-tourism, a security operations centre and a computer incident response team, with handover to the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications in September 2029
note: The company name appears as both Cybaston and Cybastion across government releases.

subject: finance.new
name: America First Global Health Strategy health data systems funding
milestone: Memorandum of understanding signed 9 December 2025
position_end: US$26,133,684 planned over 2026-2030 for health data systems including electronic medical records, a laboratory information system, disease surveillance and DHIS2, non-binding and subject to the availability of funds; the signed text commits Liberia to an open-source EMR rolled out to 100% of public health facilities by 2030 and gives the United States audit access to up to 5% of health facilities, with a data-sharing arrangement still to be negotiated and expected to run ten years, but no specimen-sharing or personal-data clause; the memorandum's text was published in March 2026 and then withdrawn, and is the subject of a federal freedom-of-information suit filed 2 April 2026 (2026-04)
note: Planned United States support across the whole memorandum is US$124,418,400 against Liberia's US$50,725,704.

subject: finance.new
name: WARDIP2 financing for Liberia
milestone: US$125m of World Bank agreements signed at Mount Coffee, 8 June 2026, of which US$50m is WARDIP2
position_end: US$50m committed for broadband, cybersecurity, digital governance and digital payments within a US$137m three-country operation (2026-06)

subject: finance.new
name: Youth Entrepreneurship Investment Bank
milestone: Put at almost US$18m by the finance minister, with a national coordinator recruited, July 2026
position_end: Almost US$18m targeting 30,000 youth-led businesses and about 100,000 jobs, with a board being constituted; no disbursement stated (2026-07)

subject: infra.connect
name: 5G network services
milestone: Stated as planned by the LTA chairman, January 2026
position_end: Plans stated with investors still being engaged; no spectrum award, licence condition or launch date published (2026-01)

subject: infra.connect
name: Domestic fibre-optic backbone extension
milestone: Extension from Buchanan toward Rivercess, Sinoe, Maryland, Grand Gedeh and Nimba reported under way
position_end: Line reported reaching Loguatuo from Monrovia with private firms extending it south-east; no route map, kilometre figure or completion date published (2026-01)

subject: infra.connect
name: ECOWAS second submarine cable (Cabo Verde, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Guinea-Bissau)
milestone: Feasibility study reviewed and approved at the ECOWAS expert workshop, Monrovia, 22-24 October 2025
position_end: Member-state experts with technical and financial partners reviewed and approved the feasibility study for a second submarine cable serving Cabo Verde, Liberia, Sierra Leone and Guinea-Bissau at a workshop organised by the ECOWAS Project Preparation and Development Unit in Monrovia, 22-24 October 2025; no route, cost, landing site or construction date is published
note: A regional project ECOWAS runs for four member states, the workshop hosted in Monrovia; the same record sits on the Cabo Verde, Sierra Leone and Guinea-Bissau ledgers. Whether it is the same project as the second landing at Buchanan this ledger holds separately is not stated by either source.

subject: infra.connect
name: Liberia Internet Exchange Point
milestone: Launched in Monrovia, 6 August 2015
position_start: Operating, hosted by the Cable Consortium of Liberia (2025-08)
position_end: Functional but under-peered: the regulator reported governance problems and limited provider participation in December 2025, with many providers still not peering, against upgraded equipment and a newly elected exchange association leadership

subject: infra.connect
name: Mobile data affordability (5GB basket against average monthly income)
milestone: Regulator's sector series, 2023-2025
position_start: 13.6 per cent of average monthly income, 2023
position_end: 12.1 per cent in 2025 against a 2 per cent benchmark; the basket price held flat at US$8 across all three years while average monthly income rose from US$59 to US$66, and the general services tax rise of April 2026 held telecommunications at 15 per cent

subject: infra.connect
name: Second submarine cable landing at Buchanan
milestone: Announced by the Posts and Telecommunications Minister at the technology summit, 21 July 2026
position_start: One submarine cable in Monrovia; a second landing at Buchanan not yet stated (2025-08)
position_end: Second landing at Buchanan sought, with partial funding stated as sourced and investors still being sought; no landing partner, cost or date published (2026-07)

subject: infra.connect
name: Starcell International Liberia licence
milestone: Universal licence and spectrum authorisation revoked with immediate effect, 22 July 2026
position_start: Licensed but not operating since 2020, under a 90-day suspension from 9 February 2026
position_end: Revoked, with spectrum, numbering and regulatory privileges reverting to the regulator (2026-07)
note: Market as estimated by Omdia at Q2 2026: Orange Liberia 3.2m subscribers, Lonestar Cell 2.3m, Libtelco 14,000.

subject: infra.connect
name: Starlink School Connect programme
milestone: About 90 of 156 schools connected
position_end: About 90 of 156 public high schools connected; no funder, cost or completion date published (2026-07)

subject: infra.connect
name: Telecoms traffic monitoring concession
milestone: Complaint over the replacement arrangement forwarded to the Anti-Corruption Commission's investigation unit, 30 July 2026
position_start: Concession with Telecom International Alliance operating, ratified by the legislature in 2022 and held valid by the Ministry of Justice in 2024 (2025-08)
position_end: Suspended, with a joint legislative committee recommending renegotiation rather than cancellation, operator funds in escrow of undisclosed amount, and a corruption complaint under investigation (2026-07)
note: No evidence has been publicly produced and no findings made in the complaint.

subject: infra.connect
name: TRANSCO CLSG spare fibre commercialisation
milestone: Regional consensus reached to commercialise spare fibre on the CLSG grid, June 2026
position_start: Sole reliance on the ACE cable landing in Monrovia, with no terrestrial redundancy agreed (2025-08)
position_end: Agreement in principle to commercialise spare fibre across Liberia, Sierra Leone, Guinea and Cote d'Ivoire; no operator, tariff or date published (2026-06)

subject: infra.store
name: Cable Consortium of Liberia colocation facility
milestone: Rack specifications published by the operator
position_end: The only Liberian facility owner publishing its own capacity: climate-controlled racks offered at 2-10U at 1kW, 24U at 3kW and 42U at 5kW at the Monrovia landing station, with uninterruptible and generator power, air conditioning and fire suppression
note: Offered rack configurations, not an installed or occupied capacity figure.

subject: infra.store
name: National data centre
milestone: Announced by the Posts and Telecommunications Minister, 21 July 2026
position_end: Announced to hold government data domestically; no site, cost, timetable or operator named (2026-07)

subject: infra.store
name: Payment-system continuity and disaster-recovery standards
milestone: Committed in the central bank's 2026 policy statement
position_start: No published continuity or backup standard (2025-08)
position_end: The central bank has undertaken to set minimum uptime, disaster-recovery and business-continuity standards for payment participants and to require regular resilience testing; the supreme audit institution separately records its own servers, networks and backup systems as fragile (2026-07)

subject: infra.store
name: Tier III+ data centre at Buchanan
milestone: Stated as under development in the National Data Governance Policy, March 2026
position_end: Stated as under development for sovereign hosting of the National Identification Registry and the Liberia Revenue Authority; no operator, cost or completion date published (2026-03)

subject: infra.energy
name: 2015 Electricity Law and the Rural Energy Fund
milestone: Enacted 23 October 2015
position_end: Puts the Rural and Renewable Energy Agency and the Rural Energy Fund on a statutory footing and requires system plans to be filed with the regulator, which published its own inventory of generation, imports, transmission assets and connections for 2024

subject: infra.energy
name: WARDIP-SOP2 environmental and social management framework
milestone: Issued December 2025
position_start: No document treating water or power at digital-infrastructure sites (2025-08)
position_end: Sets construction water-use and electrical-hazard requirements for data-centre and cable landing-station works, the only Liberian instrument addressing utilities at digital sites (2025-12)

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cybercrime Act 2025
milestone: Signed into force by the President 2026-08-19
position_end: Signed into force on 2026-08-19, seven months after the Legislature passed it and nearly nineteen months after the House's data-breach proceedings
note: the signature ends a delay the base had been carrying since January 2026, when Senate concurrence was communicated to the House. The ITU's 2024 Global Cybersecurity Index still places Liberia in its second-lowest maturity tier, which is the position the law is meant to move and has not yet moved; no commencement date, implementing regulation or enforcement body is published with it

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cybersecurity Regulations (LTA-REG-0013-2026)
milestone: Made by the LTA under the Telecommunications Act 2007, 13 January 2026, effective from the day of publication
position_end: Requires telecom providers to store personal data and PII primarily inside Liberia's own territory (s.7.3(A)(v)), establish an in-house Cybersecurity Unit within one year of the effective date (s.7.1), notify the LTA of breaches within 24 hours and customers within 72 hours (s.7.6(A)(ii)), run annual penetration testing and keep security-event logs for at least 12 months (s.7.5), and file tested incident-response and continuity plans; the LTA is to run a sector CERT with a 24/7 hotline (s.8.2). Penalties are revenue-linked (up to US$3,000 plus 0.15% of the preceding year's gross revenue for failing to establish the Unit, escalating to US$25,000 and possible licence suspension) but apply only from one year after the effective date (s.10.7); the s.10.6 penalty escalation ladder is unreadable in both held copies (2026-01)
note: The s.10.6 penalty ladder is mangled in the readable text capture and unrenderable from the regulator's own image-only scan; the 13 January 2026 date is the regulation's stated making-date, not independently confirmed as the publication date that fixes entry into force under s.12.1.

subject: infra.cybersec
name: House investigation into the 2026 data breach
milestone: Investigation ordered by the House, February 2026
position_end: Investigation ordered into an alleged breach of about 2m citizens' data across the revenue, electricity and insurance bodies; no findings published (2026-02)
note: The revenue authority denied the breach; the probe also cited the absence of a national cybersecurity strategy.

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National Cybersecurity Act
milestone: Scheduled for Q3 2025 by the cybersecurity strategy action plan
position_start: Scheduled for Q3 2025 by the strategy's action plan, not yet due (2025-08)
position_end: No draft, bill or enactment held; the data governance policy of March 2026 names only the unenacted Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act 2024 and Cybercrime Act 2025 (2026-03)
note: The base holds no record of delivery rather than a stated non-delivery.

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National Cybersecurity Council
milestone: Scheduled for Q4 2024 by the cybersecurity strategy action plan, operational basis set for Q1 2025
position_start: Scheduled for Q4 2024 by the strategy's action plan, not established (2025-08)
position_end: No constituting instrument, membership or meeting record held (2026-08)
note: The base holds no record of establishment rather than a stated non-delivery.

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National Cybersecurity Strategy 2025-2029
status: Implemented, adoption of the published text not established
milestone: Published by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, cover dated July 2024
position_start: Published, with an action plan dating deliverables from Q4 2024 (2024-07)
position_end: Published and unamended; the primary legislation its action plan scheduled for Q3 2025 is not held as delivered (2026-03)
note: Prepared by SecDev under World Bank contract. The cover reads July 2024 for a 2025-2029 period while every running header reads Draft National Cybersecurity Strategy 2024-2029, and whether the posted file is the adopted final text is not established from the document. Resolved 2026-08-10: not a genuine contradiction with the House's February 2026 call for 'a coherent national cybersecurity strategy' — that is a characterisation of non-operationalisation, not a denial the document exists; the Ministry's own March 2026 National Data Governance Policy lists the National Cybersecurity Strategy (2024-2029) among the strategies it complements, confirming existence. Adoption of the posted text remains not established.

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Directive on additional customer due diligence for non-resident customers
milestone: Signed and effective 16 February 2026
position_end: Directive CBL/FIA/001/2025 binds financial institutions to identity verification for non-resident, non-Liberian customers, addressing a deficiency named in the 2023 regional mutual evaluation (2026-02)

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Education Management Information System (EMIS 2.0)
milestone: 2025/26 school census moved to digital collection, March 2026
position_start: Paper-based first-generation system with a school-census data gap since 2021 and limited integration across sub-sectors (2025-09)
position_end: A costed three-year modernisation roadmap validated in September 2025 introduces national unique learner and teacher identifiers, and the 2025/26 national school census moved to school-based digital collection across all 15 counties and 125 districts (2026-03)

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Government Service Bus
milestone: Prototype consultancy re-tendered, February 2026
position_start: Zero of a target ten government systems exchanging data through it (2025-09)
position_end: Still zero systems as at September 2025 against a target of ten by December 2030; the firm-based prototype design and installation package was cancelled and re-issued as an individual-consultant package from February 2026 (2026-02)

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Integrated Sample Referral System framework
milestone: Framework validated, July 2026
position_start: No national framework linking sample transport to results reporting (2025-08)
position_end: A national framework linking laboratory sample transport, results reporting and disease surveillance has been validated; the ministry states adoption and implementation are still prospective (2026-07)

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Interoperability framework between government registers
milestone: Mandated by Executive Order 163, first release due within 180 days
position_start: No interoperability framework and no body owning one (2025-08)
position_end: Executive Order 163 of April 2026 creates the Office of Technology, Digitalization and Innovation as the central authority for government-wide technical standards and requires a first release of the Government Interoperability Framework within 180 days; the terms of reference for its chief technology officer assign the duty, and nothing has been published (2026-07)
note: The enterprise standards and interoperability rules Executive Order 163 provides for, or a data-sharing instrument between agencies.

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Trade information portal
milestone: Case for the portal set out by the special economic zone authority, August 2026
position_end: The special economic zone authority says a trade information portal could ease doing business; nothing is commissioned and no scope, funder or date is on file

subject: dpi.id
name: Automated Driver License and Vehicle Registration System
milestone: Launched January 2026
position_end: A state-run platform covering licence management, card printing, dispatch, audit trails and compliance monitoring, with an online renewal application and billing integration to the revenue authority (2026-01)

subject: dpi.id
name: Birth registration to national identity integration
milestone: Priorities set for 2026-2036, July 2026
position_start: Birth registration and the identity register unconnected (2025-08)
position_end: A UNICEF-supported pilot has run a point-of-birth workflow linking birth certificate, national identity number and immunisation record, and the health ministry names interoperability with the identity registry among its 2026-2036 priorities - objectives rather than achieved conditions (2026-07)

subject: dpi.id
name: Commercial motorcycle and tricycle rider registry
milestone: Memorandum signed 2026-08-16
position_end: A memorandum between the riders' union and a private digital services company to build a digital identity, GPS tracking and a rider database for commercial motorcycle and tricycle operators, aimed at curbing vehicle theft and linking informal-sector riders to formal financial and government services
note: a private arrangement covering location tracking of a working population; no data-protection basis, custodian, retention rule or consent mechanism is reported, and no statutory backing is claimed

subject: dpi.id
name: Executive Order 147 (mandatory biometric identity)
milestone: Signed April 2025, making enrolment mandatory for citizens and 90-day residents
position_start: In force, making the identification number the primary credential for banking, health, education and telecoms (2025-08)
position_end: In force and unamended, on a register whose issuance was halted for part of the period (2026-08)
sources: 2025-04-30 Liberia makes biometric ID mandatory — Executive Order 147|2025-04-30-no-national-id-no-transaction-eo147-observer

subject: dpi.id
name: Identity Query Portal and e-Verification platform
milestone: Mandated by Executive Order 147, April 2025
position_start: No general authentication service against the identity register (2025-08)
position_end: Executive Order 147 requires every public and private institution to verify against the registry database through the Identity Query Portal and the e-Verification platform, with data handling bound to Part IX of the 2011 Act (2025-04)

subject: dpi.id
name: National Biometric Identification System (NIR)
milestone: Replacement costed at US$39m 2026-08-31
position_start: Mandatory under Executive Order 147, issuance running amid a procurement dispute over a rejected restricted-bid award (2025-08)
position_end: the identification registry seeking US$39m to replace its technology and open identification centres nationwide, where biometric and personal data would be captured and cards printed the same day
note: no concession value, term, revenue model or data-protection provision is published, the registry states it will disclose the agreement only after ratification, and the suspension of mass enrolment has now run more than a year

subject: dpi.id
name: National identity documents for children under six
milestone: Inaugurated 16 January 2025
position_start: No identity document issued below the ordinary enrolment age (2025-08)
position_end: A pilot in Montserrado, Grand Bassa and Gbarpolu funded by UNICEF for an initial 5,000 children at no cost to parents, with the health ministry issuing free birth certificates alongside (2025-01)

subject: dpi.id
name: National identity enrolment
position_start: About 740,000 enrolled, under 15% of about 5.3m, at a US$5 card fee (2024-12)
position_end: About 640,000 prior registrants locked out of the system and issuance halted; no updated enrolment figure published (2026-03)
sources: 2026-03-20-national-id-rollout-held-up-1-7m-debt-fpa|2025-06-09 Liberia needs more funding to widen national ID coverage (NIR's Peters)

subject: dpi.id
name: Refugee biometric identity enrolment
milestone: Mandate extended by Executive Order 159, June 2026
position_start: Refugee identity cards provided for by the Refugee Act 1993 and issued outside the biometric register (2025-08)
position_end: A March 2026 memorandum brings eligible refugees into the National Biometric Identification System with specialised biometric refugee cards, and the refugee commission was rebranded RAMCO in June 2026 with a mandate extended to statelessness, returnees, displaced persons and migration governance (2026-06)

subject: dpi.id
name: SIM registration linked to the national identity number
milestone: Deadline of 10 July 2025 set under the LTA-NIR memorandum of October 2024
position_end: No compliance figure, enforcement action or revised deadline published since (2026-08)
sources: 2024-10-10 Liberia sets July 2025 deadline for SIM registration linked to national ID (LTA-NIR MoU)

subject: dpi.pay
name: Digital payments in revenue collection
milestone: Central bank backed the revenue authority’s collection drive, August 2026
position_start: Did not exist as a stated joint position
position_end: The central bank has backed the revenue authority’s collection drive and states that digital payments are key to fiscal sustainability; no collection figure, channel share or target is on file

subject: dpi.pay
name: Directive on routing government payments through the national switch
milestone: Effective 27 October 2025 for payments, 1 December 2025 for collections
position_start: Government mobile-money payments and collections routed outside a national switch (2025-08)
position_end: Directive CBL/E-GOV/DIR/002/2025 requires every government mobile-money payment to a beneficiary to route exclusively through the national switch from 27 October 2025, and all revenue collections by mobile money from 1 December 2025 (2026-03)

subject: dpi.pay
name: Integrated mobile money tax payment platform
milestone: Launched July 2025
position_start: Taxes paid in person or through banks (2025-08)
position_end: A mobile-money platform connected directly to the integrated tax administration system carries taxes and fees for 18 ministries and agencies over USSD without internet, with a text-message receipt (2025-07)

subject: dpi.pay
name: Interoperable payment fee regime
milestone: Central bank-approved schedule reported 5 August 2026
position_end: A single charge of no more than 1.0% of value from US$1.00 to US$2,000.00 and a flat fee of no more than US$25.00 above it, available 24 hours a day (2026-08)
note: The flat cap is regressive above about US$2,500, where it falls below 1.0% of value and keeps falling.

subject: dpi.pay
name: National Electronic Payment Switch
milestone: Named by the finance minister at a youth town hall, 28 July 2026
position_end: Provided for as the follow-on to the instant payment pilot, alongside person-to-government payments; no go-live date or budget line published (2026-07)

subject: dpi.pay
name: Pan-African Payment and Settlement System participation
milestone: Rollout 27 March 2025
position_end: Live with the central bank as Liberia's settlement agent from March 2025, with the bank's 2025 annual report recording implementation and a first series of cross-border transfers terminating into mobile wallets (2026-03)

subject: dpi.pay
name: Pay Na-Na inclusive instant payment system
milestone: Launched 16 December 2025 on Mojaloop, in 73 business days
position_start: Did not exist; mobile money split between two closed networks (2025-08)
position_end: Interoperable between Lonestar Cell MTN Mobile Money and Orange Money Liberia, covering person-to-person and government-to-person payments (2025-12). The central bank's own account is that it was built to a business case rather than to a regulation and stood up in 73 days, sequencing government payments first - moving civil-servant salaries off cheques into wallets, which gave the integrated mobile-money operators access to float - against a national target of 50% of adults holding a bank or wallet account

subject: dpi.registry
name: Biometric voter register
milestone: Preparation stated to begin January 2027
position_end: The electoral commission will first assess the viability of the 2023 roll; if a fresh exercise is needed it would be fully biometric with same-day card issue over satellite connectivity, with intensive preparation from January 2027 (2026-08)

subject: dpi.registry
name: Civil registration of births and deaths
milestone: Birth and Death Registration Policy 2026-2031 launched, 4-6 August 2026
position_start: Registration under the Bureau of Vital Statistics on a system the 2017 policy records as never fully developed (2025-08)
position_end: A successor Birth and Death Registration Policy 2026-2031 was launched at the national health review conference in August 2026, superseding the 2017 policy, with no target or budget line reported (2026-08)

subject: dpi.registry
name: Collateral registry
milestone: Regulation CBL/RSD/001/2026 gazetted 6 July 2026, repealing the 2013 regulation
position_start: A collateral registry covering movable property only, under a regulation of 2013
position_end: An enhanced registry launched on 27 August 2026 under a regulation gazetted on 6 July 2026 that repeals the 2013 instrument and extends the registry to immovable as well as movable property, with new collateral to be registered within ten working days, alongside the ongoing modernisation of the credit reference system
note: The regulation itself is now held, so the ten-working-day registration rule and the extension to immovable property can be read at source. No registration volume, fee schedule or relationship to the land registry is stated.

subject: dpi.registry
name: Enhanced collateral registry
milestone: Newly launched
position_end: A newly launched collateral registry allowing borrowing against assets lenders previously ignored. A published commentary sets it against an approaching national conference on non-performing loans, arguing that access without understanding turns financial inclusion into debt inclusion and that the measure of the registry should be whether borrowers become stronger businesses rather than how many more poor people can borrow
note: the base reaches the registry through a commentary rather than an official record: no launch date, asset classes, registration count or fee schedule is held

subject: dpi.registry
name: Liberia Household Social Registry
milestone: 442,000 households ranked, May 2026
position_start: About 442,000 records with integration to other national systems ongoing (2025-07)
position_end: Over 442,000 verified and poverty-ranked households, 35 per cent of the population, across 14 of 15 counties, with transfers delivered through mobile money (2026-05)

subject: dpi.registry
name: National digital postal address system
milestone: Rollout stated as begun across all fifteen counties, 21 July 2026
position_end: Rollout stated as begun in all fifteen counties; no completion date, budget line or addressing standard published (2026-07)

subject: dpi.registry
name: Taxpayer register
milestone: Integrated tax administration system replaced its predecessor from 1 December 2023
position_start: Transaction processing on the predecessor tax system (2025-08)
position_end: 165,608 registered taxpayers in 2024 across large, medium, government and non-profit, natural-resource, small and micro and real-property segments, with 7,662 inactive (2025-09)

subject: dpi.mis
name: ASYCUDA World customs management system
milestone: Second national time release study published, July 2026
position_start: Electronic declarations at automated ports, manual declarations elsewhere (2025-08)
position_end: Unchanged in coverage; the customs department published its second national time release study on clearance times at the Freeport of Monrovia, and a compliance audit covering 2018 to 2024 found variances between bills and payments in the customs and tax systems (2026-07)

subject: dpi.mis
name: Emergency medical services digital patient care reporting
milestone: First phase live in Montserrado, June 2026
position_end: Digitised and in use in Montserrado through the National Health Intelligence Center, the first phase of a national rollout (2026-06)

subject: dpi.mis
name: Facility-level electronic medical records
milestone: Quotation sought for two health centres, October 2025
position_start: No facility-level electronic medical record system (2025-08)
position_end: An implementation interoperable with the national health information platform was put to tender for the Careysburg and Duport Road health centres, including hardware and network setup (2025-10)
note: The tender document contradicts itself on reference number and submission deadline.

subject: dpi.mis
name: Judiciary case management system
milestone: Successor strategic plan reported, July 2026
position_start: Court administration substantially manual with an outdated docket system (2025-08)
position_end: 60 clerks and assistant clerks were trained on the upgraded case management system in 2025 and 14 tablets delivered in April 2026; a reported 2026-2030 judicial plan ties backlog reduction to an electronic case management system in all circuit courts, with electronic filing and virtual hearings, against a judicial budget stated as rising to US$33.3m in 2026 (2026-07)
note: The 2026-2030 plan text is not published; the 2024-2028 plan is the only one the base holds.

subject: dpi.mis
name: Liberia Land Information System
milestone: Valuation software fielded in Nimba, February 2026
position_start: Deed registry, cadastre and survey mandate consolidated in one authority since 2016, records substantially manual (2025-09)
position_end: A three-year framework signed in October 2025 with South Korean partners to build a digital land-records platform piloting in Montserrado and Margibi; a standardised registry-linked national deed form became mandatory in January 2026; and over 12,000 Nimba properties were mapped by February 2026 with about 10,000 sites still to assess (2026-02)

subject: dpi.mis
name: National Police Crime Statistics Information System
milestone: Launched at police headquarters, 25 January 2021
position_end: Live at police headquarters with a training group of 15 at launch; no county or depot deployment is stated in the record

subject: dpi.mis
name: STAR-P digital lending platform
status: Not held, searched 2026-08-11 - the state auditor verified in the field that the contracted system was not deployed
milestone: Management Letter issued 2026-06-29 on the audit period to 2025-10-31
position_end: Not held
note: the General Auditing Commission found US$36,768 paid in full to a savings and loans institution for a platform contractually due live by May 2025 and not deployed at its May 2026 field verification; the same audit found no functional project audit committee, a US$27,000 consultancy let without competitive procurement, and an agriculture commercialisation fund reporting dashboard never formally handed over to the ministry

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Automated telecom licensing and renewal platform
milestone: Rolled out, reported 2026-08-13
position_end: Rolled out by the telecommunications regulator, letting applicants apply and renew online while in-person service is kept available, as part of a stated shift away from paper-based licensing; no licence count, processing time or fee schedule is published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Civil Service Agency automated legal power of attorney platform
milestone: Went live December 2025 with 5,000 enrolled across 16 government entities
position_end: In service, tying civil-servant purchases to fingerprint verification against the agency database (2025-12)

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Electronic government procurement platform
milestone: Equipment handed to the telecommunications regulator, reported 2026-08-12
position_start: Launched nationally in February 2025 after a pilot with six institutions (2025-08)
position_end: Phase Two equipment distribution begun on 2026-08-05, with the telecommunications regulator receiving equipment to strengthen its use of the platform under bilateral cooperation with Sierra Leone’s procurement authorities reported on 2026-08-12; no transaction count, entity coverage or procurement value is published
note: Sierra Leone's procurement authority studied the system on 6-7 August 2026, which is the first export of a Liberian govtech system on the record.

subject: dpi.govtech
name: GREAT digital identity and digital government project
milestone: US$30m World Bank project launched, March 2025
position_start: Launched at US$30m to fund the enrolment push (2025-03)
position_end: Running, with a US$2m tranche put on hold during the identity system's debt lock; no disbursement total published (2026-03)
sources: 2025-03-24 Liberia launches DPI project (GREAT) with $30M World Bank funding|2025-01-01-world-bank-lbr-2025-liberia-great-digital-id-bw03

subject: dpi.govtech
name: National Single Window
milestone: Hardware tendered, 9 June 2026
position_start: No dedicated hosting for the trade window (2025-08)
position_end: An open international tender of June 2026 seeks 8 application servers, 4 database servers, 2 storage controllers and 2 storage arrays with Fibre Channel switching for the window shared by the revenue, agriculture, commerce and standards agencies (2026-06)

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Office of Technology, Digitalization and Innovation (Executive Order 163)
milestone: Executive Order 163 signed, 22 April 2026
position_end: Established as the whole-of-government coordinator for enterprise standards, interoperability, technical clearance of ICT investments and baseline cybersecurity, with 12 months to draft an institutionalising law (2026-04)

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Online police clearance platform
milestone: Live 1 May 2026
position_start: Manual police clearance, in use for more than 50 years (2025-08)
position_end: Live with electronic payment, application tracking, certificate verification and digital fingerprint integration, built by revenue authority programmers, with a rollout to five further regions announced (2026-05)

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Private-school operating permit system
milestone: Digitisation stated at a government press briefing 2026-08-11
position_end: Operating permits for private schools are being taken online after schools were found submitting mismatched teacher-qualification records, alongside geographic mapping of schools completed in five counties with donor support to extend it to ten more
note: the account is the education minister's; no platform name, cost or completion date is stated

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Regional tax administration capacity project
milestone: Launched 2026-08-18 with Liberia among six beneficiaries
position_end: A regional tax administration forum project on a grant of about US$5.3m from a development fund's transition support facility, with Liberia among six West African beneficiaries
note: the national allocation and the digital component are not itemised

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Revenue authority corporate strategic plan 2025-2029
milestone: Launched 2026-08-20
position_end: A five-year plan whose fourth goal is automation and data-driven decision-making, set out in four objectives covering system uptime and ICT risk on the tax and customs platforms, enterprise management software for internal support functions, ICT governance, and integrated online self-service for taxpayers, against a stated deployment of the customs system to 11 of 17 customs business offices and the tax administration system to five sites
note: the plan text is now held, as an OCR sidecar over an image-only PDF; it is internally inconsistent about its own span, one methodology section calling it 2024-2028 against 2025-2029 everywhere else, and it succeeds a first plan that expired unreplaced

subject: digital.localgov
name: Digitalisation of county and city administration
milestone: Nine of fifteen county planning units equipped, March 2026
position_start: 35 of 135 computers supplied to the county service centres in 2015 still functional, with no printers, no internet connectivity and unstable power (2025-01)
position_end: Equipment reached five more county development planning units in March 2026, bringing nine of fifteen counties covered with six pending, and a World Bank-financed tender of June 2026 seeks 38 laptops, 57 desktops, 52 uninterruptible supplies, a high-end server and 17 rugged tablets for the Monrovia and Paynesville city corporations (2026-06)
note: A county or municipal digital plan, a local service platform, or an administration report on digital service delivery.

subject: tech.ai
name: Automated Decision Management System for climate services
milestone: Consultancy re-advertised, April 2026
position_start: No government instrument specifying artificial intelligence inside a sectoral information system (2025-08)
position_end: A cloud-based automated decision system for the US$11,431,969 climate information project is at procurement, with a minimum viable product in pilot counties before a 15-county rollout; the agriculture ministry separately held a generative-AI design workshop for extension services against its own ratio of one extension officer to more than 40,000 farmers (2026-04)

subject: tech.ai
name: CJ Lewis legal-learning artificial intelligence
milestone: Launched at a Monrovia press conference, 31 July 2026
position_end: In service over Supreme Court opinions from 1861 to 2026 plus statutes and regulations, built by a private law library with OHCHR support (2026-07)
note: Claims are the developer's own: no accuracy or evaluation figure is given, no model or vendor is named, and the corpus is a private compilation rather than an official publication of Liberian law.

subject: tech.ai
name: Lorpu AI information service
milestone: Launched July 2026
position_end: A text-message AI query service at L$0.5 a subscription, usable without a smartphone or a data plan; an operator product, with the schools tie-in a pledge rather than an agreement (2026-07)

subject: tech.ai
name: National artificial intelligence priority
milestone: Accepted in principle by the President at the youth town hall, July 2026
position_end: Accepted in principle, conditioned on applications in agriculture, transport and commerce; no policy, institution, budget line or date attached (2026-07)
note: The proposal came from the President's Youth Advisory Council, not from the executive.

subject: tech.industry
name: Smart ports memorandum with HAROPA PORT
milestone: Memorandum signed in Le Havre, July 2026
position_end: Non-exclusive memorandum covering all four seaports across five areas including automated terminal operations; no commitment amount, implementation date or named system (2026-07)

subject: tech.innovate
name: Lantern GovTech and Cyber Arena platform
milestone: Won the national Startup World Cup at the technology summit, 22 July 2026
position_end: Operating and selected to represent Liberia at the global final, pitched on domestic data custody; the firm projects a US$20m return over five years and plans a domestic security operations centre (2026-07)
note: The firm reports that over 95% of local graduates at its Monrovia competition lacked practical international-standard defence skills; a vendor claim, not an independent audit.

subject: tech.innovate
name: LiYEPA entrepreneurship accelerator
milestone: Opened 30 June 2026
position_end: A six-month accelerator targeting 100 to 120 innovators, 10 market-ready prototypes and five small enterprises at up to US$8,000 each on milestone-based release, with 40 per cent women-led (2026-07)

subject: tech.innovate
name: UNIPOD innovation and digital hub
milestone: Named by UNDP as a flagship contribution at the technology summit, July 2026
position_end: Operating under UNDP Africa's Timbuktoo platform; no commitment amount disclosed (2026-07)

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Civil Service Agency Strategic Plan 2025-2029
milestone: Launched 9 April 2025
position_start: No standing instrument for civil-service digital literacy (2025-08)
position_end: The plan places digital-literacy enhancement under its capacity-building pillar and records the Civil Service Training Center; a first structured artificial-intelligence programme for ministry officials followed in November 2025, and the agency put a biometric-verified benefits platform in front of every public employee (2025-11)

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Media and information literacy training for elections
milestone: First of three sessions held in Monrovia, 31 July 2026
position_end: 19 young leaders trained in the first of three sessions, run by UNDP with the elections commission and press union on Canadian funding; no budget disclosed (2026-07)

subject: capacity.literacy
name: MOE Digital Learning Platform and Liberia Learns
milestone: Rolled out by the Ministry of Education, 6 January 2026
position_end: In service for Grades 1 to 3 through curriculum-aligned video, audio and radio in local languages, with sign-language interpretation on video lessons (2026-01)
sources: 2026-01-07 Digital driving licence coming to South Africa

subject: capacity.training
name: Frontier Tech Leaders machine learning bootcamp
milestone: First cohort graduated 28 January 2026
position_start: Four of about 30 tertiary institutions offering IT-related bachelor's programmes, no IT master's degree available, and no national series counting ICT graduates entering digital employment (2020-01)
position_end: 387 applications and 41 completions on a three-month machine learning bootcamp hosted by the University of Liberia, with 200 more trained in advanced Python, cybersecurity and data engineering; no graduate-outcome tracking exists to say where they went (2026-02)

subject: capacity.training
name: Senior secondary education technology deployment
milestone: First School Connect link opened at Kakata, April 2026
position_start: 156 public and community senior secondary schools across all 15 counties equipped with laptops, projectors, learning-management devices and solar power, and 50 trainers cascading to 300 teachers (2024-10)
position_end: The first School Connect installation opened at the Booker Washington Institute in April 2026, beginning a rollout the regulator states will reach 155 public high schools (2026-04)

subject: capacity.training
name: University of Liberia master's programme in artificial intelligence
milestone: Partnership announced by UNDP, reported 3 August 2026
position_end: Announced as the country's first such programme; no start date, intake or funding amount disclosed (2026-08)

subject: capacity.research
name: Domestic digital research capacity
milestone: Master's programme design pack produced, November 2025
position_start: Four of about 30 tertiary institutions offering IT-related bachelor's programmes and no IT master's degree available (2020-01)
position_end: A three-day university workshop in November 2025 produced a design pack for Liberia's first master's programme in artificial intelligence, and an independent think tank published its own monitoring of the government's digital commitments covering biometric identity, electronic procurement and digital government (2026-01)
note: A university research programme, a published national research output, or an institutional mandate for digital research.

subject: include.access
name: Account ownership and mobile wallets
position_start: 52% account ownership with more than 11m wallets (2024)
position_end: No later figure published (2026-08)

subject: include.access
name: Disability data and the National Commission on Disabilities
milestone: First treaty-body review concluded, 6 May 2026
position_start: Functional-difficulty prevalence published from the 2022 census, with no administrative disability register (2024-06)
position_end: The commission launched a 2026-2030 plan proposing a research and data management department and a monitoring framework, and the treaty body concluded Liberia's first review in May 2026 recording that no replies to the list of issues were submitted and that the state did not attend the dialogue (2026-05)

subject: include.access
name: Freedom of Information Act 2010
milestone: Enacted 2010
position_end: In force: it defines documents to include electronic records, allows requests by electronic mail and constitutes the Independent Information Commissioner; a two-day multi-stakeholder consultation in November 2025 brought civil society, academia, the private sector and the media into drafting the National Data Policy

subject: include.access
name: Women's share of counted digital-skills cohorts
milestone: Operator and programme reporting, 2025-2026
position_end: 3 women among 41 machine-learning bootcamp graduates and 18 women graduating in Python from 204 trained in foundational artificial intelligence, against 36.74 per cent female participation among 3,035 operator training beneficiaries in 2025; the regional digital project sets a target of about 30,000 officials trained at 40 per cent women

subject: include.divides
name: Internet penetration
position_start: 1.84m internet users, 32.4% of a 5.67m population, with about 3.8m offline (2025-01)
position_end: No later national figure published (2026-08)

subject: data.statistics
name: Census and national survey programme
milestone: 2024 agriculture survey microdata released, July 2026
position_start: Final results of the 2022 population and housing census as the standing demographic baseline (2023-06)
position_end: The first annual agriculture survey after the 2024 agriculture census used tablet-based collection with satellite location checks, and its public-use microdata and an attached first women's empowerment and nutrition module were released through the statistics office's own catalogue (2026-07)

subject: data.statistics
name: National Strategy for the Development of Statistics III (2026-2030)
milestone: Signed at Monrovia, 15 December 2025
position_end: A third national statistical strategy signed in December 2025 for 2026-2030 on three pillars, followed a month later by the first national diagnostic of how the statistical system serves and fails its users (2026-01)

subject: data.statistics
name: Statistics compiled from administrative records
milestone: Fourth volume published, December 2023
position_end: A standing compilation of official statistics drawn from ministry and agency administrative records for 2016 to 2022, the base's evidence that Liberia produces statistics from administrative data at all

subject: data.open
name: National open data policy
status: Not held, searched 2026-09-04 - no adopted open-data instrument located
milestone: No instrument found
position_end: Still none; the statistics office publishes anonymised public-use microdata under stated access conditions, resting on the confidentiality provisions of the 2004 statistics Act rather than an open-data instrument (2026-02)

subject: data.open
name: Publication of the telecoms regulator's own revenue
milestone: Disclosure refused again 2026-08-31
position_end: the regulator's board chairman again declining to say what the international gateway monitoring system has earned, with the dispute now carrying a legal edge
note: The Authority's licensing fees, spectrum charges, regulatory levies and numbering receipts, or an audited account of them from the General Auditing Commission.

subject: data.satellite
name: Earth observation or geospatial data programme
milestone: Nationwide soil mapping begun, May 2026
position_start: No national earth-observation or geospatial programme on the record (2025-08)
position_end: A national forest reference level submitted in January 2026 reads a 4km systematic sample of 5,990 plots from Sentinel-2, Landsat, MODIS and Planet imagery for 2020 to 2024; farm-level geolocation traceability for cocoa, coffee, rubber and palm oil has at least US$530,000 committed against the EU deforestation regulation; and a nationwide soil mapping campaign began in Bong County in May 2026 (2026-05)
note: A national geospatial or earth-observation programme document, or an agency mandate covering satellite data.

subject: data.satellite
name: Meteosat Third Generation receiving station
milestone: Installed at Roberts International Airport, 24 October 2025
position_start: No compliant surface observation network, one operational staffed station and no transmission to the global system, with the earlier satellite reception workstation underused for power and connectivity (2024-04)
position_end: A receiving station for Meteosat Third Generation model data and high-resolution imagery installed in October 2025, EU-funded and installed under African Union Commission contract (2025-10)

subject: data.satellite
name: National Spatial Data Infrastructure
milestone: Taken to the 16th UN-GGIM session, August 2026
position_end: Taken by the Land Authority to the United Nations' sixteenth global geospatial information management session in New York, where it sought international partnerships and technical support to build a coordinated geospatial framework for land administration, mapping and national planning
note: an approach for support rather than a programme; no funding, custodian, standard or timetable is stated

subject: geopol.china
name: Belt and Road Initiative memorandum of understanding
milestone: Signed 27 April 2019
position_start: Framework memorandum signed 2019, no digital project named under it (2025-08)
position_end: Liberia's first Digital Village opened in Lofa County in May 2026 under a partnership of the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, the LTA and Huawei, with no signed instrument, value or duration published (2026-05)

subject: geopol.eu
name: European Union digital cooperation with Liberia
status: Implemented, the flagship instrument proposed for termination
milestone: Termination proposed, 9 September 2025
position_start: The EU-Liberia forest partnership agreement in force since December 2013, requiring a chain-of-custody information system and legality assurance database for timber licensing (2012-07)
position_end: The Commission proposed terminating the agreement in September 2025 after a decade without an operative licensing scheme, a proposal rather than an adopted termination; EU funding separately delivered the satellite receiving station installed in October 2025 (2025-09)
note: A Global Gateway or EU delegation announcement, a financing agreement, or a programme document naming Liberia.

subject: geopol.gulf
name: Gulf state digital investment in Liberia
note: An investment agreement, data-centre or connectivity commitment from a Gulf sovereign fund or operator.

subject: geopol.india
name: Indian digital cooperation with Liberia
note: A bilateral memorandum, a line-of-credit agreement, or an India Stack or ITEC programme document naming Liberia.
